events.title: VMware Workstation 1.0 released
events.summary: VMware shipped Workstation 1.0 on May 15, 1999 — desktop software that ran multiple x86 operating systems in virtual machines.
events.about: VMware let developers test on Linux, Windows, and BSD simultaneously on one PC — no rebooting, no spare hardware. It pioneered x86 binary translation and later hardware-assisted virtualization. DevOps teams later built on the same hypervisor lineage for ESXi and cloud VMs; Docker containers addressed a different layer, but VMware defined how backend devs thought about isolation.

narrative.whyChosen: VMware Workstation brought practical x86 virtualization to developer desktops.
narrative.whyImportant: It made cross-platform testing and server simulation routine before cloud VMs were ubiquitous.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed to run multiple OS environments without maintaining separate physical machines.
